newsitem.title: HONG KONG: World stock exchange body to discuss China entry.
newsitem.headline: World stock exchange body to discuss China entry.

text.p: The International Federation of Stock Exchanges (FIBV) said it will discuss the entry of Chinese markets into the body during the next few days.
The body changed its statutes during a two-day General Assembly here so that more than one stock exchange from a particular country could be a full member.

The Stock Exchange of Hong Kong is a member and FIBV has been in contact with the Shenzhen and Shanghai stock exchanges for several years. "There are about 15 objective parameters which have to be complied with," said FIBV secretary general Gerrit de Marez Oyens.
"We did not even yet start the whole network for collecting the data to find out whether they comply," he said of Shanghai and Shenzhen.
The FIBV will hold an international seminar in Beijing on Thursday following a two-day General Assembly in Hong Kong.

During the General Assembly, the Irish Stock Exchange, the Lima Stock Exchange and the Lisbon Stock Exchange were elected members. The FIBV now has 51 full members, representing over 97 percent of the world stock exchange market capitalisation.

Manuel Robleda, chairman of the board of the Bolsa Mexicana de Valores, was elected president of the FIBV during the two-day meeting, replacing Bengt Ryden, president and chief executive officer of the Stockholm Stock Exchange, whose two-year term ends in February 1997.
Stock Exchange of Hong Kong chairman Edgar Cheng was elected vice president of the organisation.
